title: Graceful Shutdown, Readiness, and Live Traffic
description: Drain ongoing requests and close dependencies within a bounded shutdown window.

blocks.title: Graceful Shutdown, Readiness, and Live Traffic
blocks.content:
On SIGTERM, mark the replica unready, stop taking new work, and let ongoing operations finish within a grace period. An orchestrator may take time to route traffic away. Keep shutdown idempotent and coordinate this window with deployment settings.

Drain HTTP requests before closing a database pool they still use. Track upgraded connections and background jobs separately when they have their own lifecycle. Keep a bounded force-close path so a stuck client cannot block deployment forever.
keyPoints: Design shutdown in ownership order and test it under real traffic and stuck-client conditions.
The code handles the HTTP server only. In a deployed service, readiness, long-lived connections, jobs, and pools each need an explicit owner.

blocks.title: Run as shutdown.mjs and send SIGTERM to the process
blocks.explanation: The code handles the HTTP server only. In a deployed service, readiness, long-lived connections, jobs, and pools each need an explicit owner.

blocks.title: Interview question
blocks.question: What is the difference between readiness and liveness?
blocks.answer: Readiness indicates whether traffic should be routed to the instance. Liveness indicates whether the process should be restarted. They can intentionally differ during startup or shutdown.
blocks.explanation: The code handles the HTTP server only. In a deployed service, readiness, long-lived connections, jobs, and pools each need an explicit owner.

blocks.title: Tricky question
blocks.question: Does adding a SIGTERM listener automatically stop acceptance or let requests drain?
blocks.answer: No. The listener changes how the process responds to the signal. Application code must stop admission, await or bound outstanding work, and release owned resources.
hints: A signal notifies the application. What code owns the server lifecycle?
blocks.explanation:
The code handles the HTTP server only. In a deployed service, readiness, long-lived connections, jobs, and pools each need an explicit owner.

[Further reading](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#serverclosecallback)

blocks.title: Production scenario
blocks.question: Deployments cut active downloads even with multiple replicas. What would you verify?
blocks.answer: Verify readiness propagation and termination grace, test with an in-flight download during rollout, and measure how many responses complete. Align proxy and app limits, and consider resumable exports for actions longer than the grace window.
blocks.explanation: Design shutdown in ownership order and test it under real traffic and stuck-client conditions.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.mistake: Calling process.exit immediately from the signal handler.
blocks.whyItHappens: Immediate process termination prevents outstanding responses and cleanup from finishing.
blocks.correctApproach: Design shutdown in ownership order and test it under real traffic and stuck-client conditions.

blocks.title: Best practice
blocks.content:
Design shutdown in ownership order and test it under real traffic and stuck-client conditions.

The code handles the HTTP server only. In a deployed service, readiness, long-lived connections, jobs, and pools each need an explicit owner.

blocks.content:

title: Environment Configuration and Secret Handling
description: Validate configuration at startup and make environment differences explicit.

blocks.title: Environment Configuration and Secret Handling
blocks.content:
Environment variables are text values. Parse booleans explicitly, check numeric bounds, and report missing required configuration at startup. Keep environment access in one module so tests and consumers receive typed settings.

Node can load an env file through supported CLI options. Production configuration is typically injected by the deployment environment. Store secrets securely and keep them out of logs, fixture snapshots, and source control. Define precedence and test it.
keyPoints: Validate types and bounds once, and expose only nonsecret configuration when diagnosing startup.
An invalid supplied setting should fail startup. The default is for absent values only.

blocks.title: Run as configuration.mjs
blocks.explanation: An invalid supplied setting should fail startup. The default is for absent values only.

blocks.title: Interview question
blocks.question: Why validate configuration during startup?
blocks.answer: A configuration error can be detected before becoming a production request failure. A startup failure with a safe message gives operators a concrete signal and keeps readiness accurate.
blocks.explanation: An invalid supplied setting should fail startup. The default is for absent values only.

blocks.title: Tricky question
blocks.question: Is Boolean(process.env.FEATURE_REPORTS) false when the configured value is the string false?
blocks.answer: No. A nonempty string is truthy. Compare against documented allowed values, and decide how absent or invalid values are handled.
hints: Apply JavaScript truthiness to the actual type returned by process.env.
blocks.explanation:
An invalid supplied setting should fail startup. The default is for absent values only.

[Further reading](https://nodejs.org/api/environment_variables.html)

blocks.title: Production scenario
blocks.question: A flag enables reports in test and unexpectedly in production despite being set to false. What do you change?
blocks.answer: Centralize typed parsing, test absent and malformed values, and log a safe startup inventory of feature states. Roll out the fix with an explicit regression test.
blocks.explanation: Validate types and bounds once, and expose only nonsecret configuration when diagnosing startup.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.mistake: Printing the entire environment while debugging deployment differences.
blocks.whyItHappens: An environment dump can expose credentials or service tokens to people with log access.
blocks.correctApproach: Validate types and bounds once, and expose only nonsecret configuration when diagnosing startup.

blocks.title: Best practice
blocks.content:
Validate types and bounds once, and expose only nonsecret configuration when diagnosing startup.

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.content:
Validate configuration at startup and make environment differences explicit. A configuration error can be detected before becoming a production request failure. A startup failure with a safe message gives operators a concrete signal and keeps readiness accurate.

title: Server-Side Authorization for Multi-Tenant APIs
description: Enforce identity and tenant-level permissions in the Node API.

blocks.title: Server-Side Authorization for Multi-Tenant APIs
blocks.content:
Authentication establishes a verified identity. Authorization decides whether that identity can act on a resource. Apply those decisions on the server, with membership and policy data trusted by the server. Angular route guards and menu visibility support the user experience.

Scope reads and writes to verified tenant or account context. Avoid building a shared cache keyed only by resource ID for tenant-scoped content. For work that runs later, define which authorization must be rechecked before execution or delivery.
keyPoints: Keep authorization policy testable and cover cross-tenant, revoked-access, and stale-cache cases.
Make allow and deny behavior explicit for each resource action, including downloads and jobs that execute later.

blocks.title: Run as tenant-policy.mjs. The principal represents claims already verified by authentication middleware.
blocks.explanation: Make allow and deny behavior explicit for each resource action, including downloads and jobs that execute later.

blocks.title: Interview question
blocks.question: Where should resource ownership be enforced?
blocks.answer: At the API's access boundary and, where possible, also in scoped data queries. Every transport or task entry point that can access the resource needs a consistent policy.
blocks.explanation: Make allow and deny behavior explicit for each resource action, including downloads and jobs that execute later.

blocks.title: Tricky question
blocks.question: If a request carries a valid identity token, is it authorized for every resource belonging to the user's organization?
blocks.answer: No. Authentication and resource authorization are separate. Verify tenant scope, permissions, and resource-specific rules on the server for the operation in question.
hints: Separate proof of identity from permission to act.
blocks.explanation:
Make allow and deny behavior explicit for each resource action, including downloads and jobs that execute later.

[Further reading](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

blocks.title: Production scenario
blocks.question: An authorized manager schedules a report and loses that access before download. What behavior would you design?
blocks.answer: Record ownership and policy context for the job, then enforce the current download policy when serving the artifact. Decide deliberately whether long-running work should also be cancelled or rechecked if entitlement is withdrawn.
blocks.explanation: Keep authorization policy testable and cover cross-tenant, revoked-access, and stale-cache cases.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.mistake: Trusting tenant identifiers supplied by the browser as proof of membership.
blocks.whyItHappens: The client can supply any account identifier. Trusted authentication and server policy determine whether it can access that account.
blocks.correctApproach: Keep authorization policy testable and cover cross-tenant, revoked-access, and stale-cache cases.

blocks.title: Best practice
blocks.content:
Keep authorization policy testable and cover cross-tenant, revoked-access, and stale-cache cases.

Make allow and deny behavior explicit for each resource action, including downloads and jobs that execute later.

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.content:
Enforce identity and tenant-level permissions in the Node API. At the API's access boundary and, where possible, also in scoped data queries. Every transport or task entry point that can access the resource needs a consistent policy.

[Further reading](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)
